category_title: Mainstream students who resist specific digital tasks
minimal_context: The student is in their first lesson of the class and is receiving instructions to complete a blog post for homework.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Welcome to our first lesson. Let's discuss the homework assignment.

STUDENT: Are we going to have a choice in what we do?

TUTOR: I will go over the instructions now.

STUDENT: (Appears uncomfortable with the task being introduced)

TUTOR: I am asking everyone to complete a blog post for homework, and...

STUDENT: I’m not doing it. I don’t do blog posts.

options.A: Provide a clear beginning and end for the blog post assignment when introducing the homework task.
options.B: Break the blog post assignment down into smaller chunks so the student can complete the homework task.
options.C: Smile and state that the student can email the response instead, then open this alternative option up to the entire class.
options.D: Clarify any misconceptions about the blog post instructions and re-teach the procedural steps for the homework task.
